Technical details The root cause is CWE-116 (Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output): XmlLayout fails to sanitize characters forbidden by the XML 1.0 specification before writing log output, meaning any log message or MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context) value containing such characters produces invalid XML. The exploitation mechanics differ by StAX implementation: with the JRE built-in StAX, forbidden characters are silently written to output, producing malformed XML that conforming parsers must reject with a fatal error; with alternative StAX implementations such as Woodstox (a transitive dependency of the Jackson XML Dataformat module), an exception is thrown during the logging call and the log event is never delivered to its intended appender. The fix, implemented in pull request #4077, introduces a SanitizingXmlFactory/SanitizingWriter wrapper that replaces invalid XML 1.0 code points with the Unicode replacement character (U+FFFD) before output (Github Advisory, Log4j PR #4077). Impact The primary impact is on log integrity and availability of log data in downstream processing systems. When exploited with the JRE built-in StAX, malformed XML output causes conforming XML parsers to reject entire log documents with a fatal error, potentially causing log-processing systems to silently drop affected records — a significant concern for audit trails and security monitoring. When Woodstox or similar alternative StAX implementations are in use, the logging call itself throws an exception, meaning the log event is never delivered to its intended appender, resulting in complete loss of that log event. The impact depends on the StAX implementation in use: * JRE built-in StAX: Forbidden characters are silently written to the output, producing malformed XML. Conforming parsers must reject such documents with a fatal error, which may cause downstream log-processing systems to drop the affected records. * Alternative StAX implementations (e.g., Woodstox https://github.com/FasterXML/woodstox , a transitive dependency of the Jackson XML Dataformat module): An exception is thrown during the logging call, and the log event is never delivered to its intended appender, only to Log4j's internal status logger. Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4j Core 2.25.4, which corrects this issue by sanitizing forbidden characters before XML output.
